commits.message:
fix(packaging): declare the Node floor the install tree actually requires (rich-packaging-k9t)

`package.json#engines.node` read `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0` — character for
character the range `vite` declares. `vite` is a devDependency, so no consumer
receives it, and the published package was refusing Node 20.0-20.18, all of
21.x, and 22.0-22.11 on the authority of a build tool those consumers never
install. It now reads `>=20`, which is what `string-width` declares — the only
hard runtime dependency, and the only package in the default install tree
asking for more than Node 18.

The floor is now derived rather than asserted. `test/seam/node-floor.ts` reads
`package-lock.json`, npm's own record of which packages a default install puts
on disk and what each declares, finds the strictest range among them, and
requires `engines.node` to denote exactly that set. It has no allow-list and no
`why` field, unlike the seam rules around it, because there is no human claim
left for one to justify.

The comparison is `semver.subset`, not a check on minimum versions, and that
decides a real case: `subset(">=20.19.0", "^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0")` is false,
because 21.x satisfies the first and not the second. Comparing minimums calls
those equivalent and passes — on exactly the disjoint range shape that caused
this bug. `semver` and `@types/semver` join devDependencies for it; the
production tree is unchanged and `string-width` remains the only hard
dependency.

Four copies of this one fact existed and gave three answers: the field as
above, README.md 20, docs/introduction.md 18, and CLAUDE.md 20 while correctly
naming the field as the authority. `docs/introduction.md` is corrected, and the
rule now reads both documents back and checks the version they name against the
field. A fifth copy turned up in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which restated the
old range in a comment and credited it to a transitive dependency — both halves
false by the time anyone read them, and both removed.

That workflow takes its Node from this field via `node-version-file`, so the
change was checked against a real run rather than reasoned about: setup-node
resolves a range to its newest satisfying version, logging `Resolved
package.json as ^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0` and then taking 24.20.0. Widening the
floor does not lower CI's Node, and CI never exercised the floor in the first
place.

Verified by packing the tarball and installing it into an empty project under
Node 20.18.0 with `engine-strict=true`: the old range fails EBADENGINE, the new
one installs and renders a Table and a Panel with the expected text. CI cannot
stand in for that check, which is filed as rich-packaging-8b7.

lint clean on all three passes; 2454 tests across 84 files; docs:build clean.

perf(packaging)!: make the template engine an optional peer (rich-packaging-1xv.dpo) (#123)

@promptctl/go-template-js was a hard runtime dependency, so every consumer
installed it and its transitive @noble/hashes whether or not they ever
authored a template. The template-bindings subpath already kept it out of
the default bundle; this takes it out of the default install. Same move
rich-packaging-1xv.5 made for mobx, and the last child of that epic.

It is now a peer dependency marked optional in peerDependenciesMeta, the
pair that makes npm neither fetch the package nor warn about its absence.
optionalDependencies would not have: npm installs those. A bare peer would
not have either, since npm 7+ auto-installs peers. It stays in
devDependencies so this checkout's tests and demos still run.

Measured by packing a tarball into an empty project rather than by reading
package.json: the installed tree drops from 8 entries to 6, the two that
leave being @promptctl/go-template-js and its transitive @noble/hashes, with
no peer warning in either state. The barrel renders a Table with both peers
absent; @promptctl/rich-js/template-bindings fails at import with
ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND until the engine is installed, and renders bold-green
output through createRichTextEngine once it is. All 10 demo bundles still
boot in Chromium under playwright, and the 130 template-bindings tests that
import the engine directly still pass.

PEER_PROVIDERS gains one row naming @promptctl/rich-js/template-bindings.
The gate was confirmed red before being trusted, both ways it should go:
with the row missing it named src/template-bindings/index.ts:37, and with an
import of the engine staged into src/core/measure.ts it named the file, the
line, and the chain src/index.ts -> src/core/measure.ts. Note it reported
one reach, not five — the other four imports of the engine are `import
type` and erase, which is the runtime-graph distinction working.

The "what each published subpath costs to install" block stated mobx's
contract concretely and would have under-described the new one. Its two
cases are now one it.each over a literal table, plus a pin asserting that
table covers every optional peer package.json declares, so a third peer has
to arrive with its contract written out instead of silently undescribed.
The values stay hand-written on purpose: deriving them from PEER_PROVIDERS
would restate the gate above rather than state the contract it protects.

Three prose claims this falsifies, none of which any test reads — nothing in
the suite globs README.md, and symbol-existence.test.ts checks symbols, not
dependency claims:

  - docs/template-bindings.md: "The engine is a dependency of rich-js, so
    there is nothing extra to install."
  - README.md: "a plain dependency and arrives with the package, so that
    subpath needs nothing extra."
  - README.md: "The widget layer's MobX is the one dependency you install
    yourself" — now false because there are two. The ticket had not spotted
    this one.

The two subpaths are symmetric as of this change, which lifts the reason
the Entry points table deliberately had no "what you must install" column:
the asymmetry a row shape could have flattened is gone, so the table gains
the column and answers the question per row.

CLAUDE.md's optional-peer section named mobx alone, which would have told an
agent the engine was a plain dependency it could import from src/core/ —
exactly the hazard that gate exists to catch, and invisible here because the
package is still in devDependencies. It now covers both peers with one rule
rather than two copies of it. Its "Node >= 20 (transitively required by
@promptctl/go-template-js)" attribution is also dropped: the engine no
longer binds a default install at all. What the real floor should be is a
separate question — package.json#engines is character-for-character vite's,
a devDependency no consumer installs, while string-width, now the only hard
dependency, asks only for >=20 — and is filed rather than resolved here.

BREAKING CHANGE: consumers of @promptctl/rich-js/template-bindings must now
install @promptctl/go-template-js themselves — `npm install
@promptctl/rich-js @promptctl/go-template-js`.
